q: Which term of the A.P. 7, 11, 15, … is 95?
x: aₙ = 7 + (n − 1) × 4 = 95 gives n − 1 = 22, so n = 23. Check: a₂₃ = 7 + 88 = 95. Stopping at n − 1 = 22 gives the 22nd term, which is 91.

q: What is the sum of all two-digit numbers that leave remainder 1 when divided by 4?
x: The numbers are 13, 17, …, 97, an A.P. with d = 4 and n = (97 − 13)/4 + 1 = 22 terms. Sum = 22 × (13 + 97)/2 = 11 × 110 = 1210. Forgetting the +1 in the count gives 21 terms and 1155.

q: In an A.P., the sum of the first 10 terms is 120 and the sum of the first 20 terms is 440. What is the common difference?
x: S₁₀ = 5(2a + 9d) = 120 gives 2a + 9d = 24; S₂₀ = 10(2a + 19d) = 440 gives 2a + 19d = 44. Subtracting, 10d = 20, so d = 2 (and a = 3). Check: S₁₀ = 5(6 + 18) = 120.

q: The angles of a triangle are in A.P. and the smallest angle is 40°. What is the largest angle?
x: Write the angles as a − d, a, a + d. Their sum 3a = 180°, so a = 60°; a − d = 40° gives d = 20°, and the largest is 80°. Check: 40° + 60° + 80° = 180°. 60° is the middle angle.

q: A loan of Rs. 3250 is repaid in monthly instalments: Rs. 20 in the first month, and each month Rs. 15 more than the month before. How many months does it take?
For which value of x are x + 1, 2x + 1 and 4x − 1 consecutive terms of an A.P.?
x: The middle term is the arithmetic mean of its neighbours: 2(2x + 1) = (x + 1) + (4x − 1), so 4x + 2 = 5x and x = 2. Check: the terms are 3, 5, 7 with difference 2.

q: How many terms of the A.P. 20, 17, 14, … are positive?
x: aₙ = 20 − 3(n − 1) = 23 − 3n > 0 gives n < 23/3 ≈ 7.7, so n = 1 to 7. Check: a₇ = 2 and a₈ = −1. Rounding 7.7 up gives 8.

q: For which value of k are k, 2k + 2 and 3k + 3 three consecutive terms of a G.P.?
x: (2k + 2)² = k(3k + 3), i.e. 4(k + 1)² = 3k(k + 1). k = −1 gives −1, 0, 0, and a G.P. cannot contain 0, so divide by k + 1: 4k + 4 = 3k and k = −4. Check: −4, −6, −9 has ratio 3/2.

q: What is the 7th term of the G.P. √2, 2, 2√2, … ?
x: a = √2 and r = 2/√2 = √2, so a₇ = ar⁶ = √2 × (√2)⁶ = √2 × 8 = 8√2. Check: the terms run √2, 2, 2√2, 4, 4√2, 8, 8√2. Using r⁷ gives 16.

q: An infinite geometric series has first term 5 and sum 15. What is its common ratio?
x: S = a/(1 − r) gives 15 = 5/(1 − r), so 1 − r = 1/3 and r = 2/3. Check: 5/(1/3) = 15. Taking 1 − r = 2/3 gives 1/3, and r = 3 has no sum to infinity.

q: A culture starts with 500 bacteria, and the number doubles every 20 minutes. How many bacteria are there after 2 hours?
x: 2 hours is 6 periods of 20 minutes, so the count is 500 × 2⁶ = 500 × 64 = 32000. These counts form a G.P. 500, 1000, 2000, …, and after 6 doublings it is the 7th term. Using 2⁷ gives 64000.

q: In an infinite G.P. with positive terms, every term is twice the sum of all the terms that follow it. What is the common ratio?
x: The terms after a are ar, ar², …, with sum ar/(1 − r). So a = 2ar/(1 − r), giving 1 − r = 2r and r = 1/3. Check with 1, 1/3, 1/9, …: the terms after 1 sum to (1/3)/(2/3) = 1/2, and twice that is 1.

q: The 3rd term of a G.P. is 2. What is the product of its first five terms?
x: The first five terms are a₃/r², a₃/r, a₃, a₃r, a₃r², whose product is a₃⁵ = 2⁵ = 32. Check with 1/2, 1, 2, 4, 8: product 32. Adding instead of multiplying the powers gives 10.

q: What is the sum of the first n terms of 0.7 + 0.77 + 0.777 + … ?
Nonzero numbers a, b, c are such that 1/a, 1/b, 1/c form an A.P. with nonzero common difference. Then a, b, c form
o: both an A.P. and a G.P.
x: By definition a sequence is harmonic when the reciprocals of its terms are in A.P., so a, b, c are in H.P. For example 1/a, 1/b, 1/c = 1, 2, 3 gives 1, 1/2, 1/3, which is neither an A.P. nor a G.P.

q: Which term of the H.P. 1/2, 2/9, 1/7, … is 1/27?
x: The reciprocals 2, 9/2, 7 form an A.P. with d = 5/2. Solve 2 + (n − 1)(5/2) = 27: n − 1 = 10, so n = 11. Check: 2 + 25 = 27. Stopping at n − 1 gives the 10th.

q: A, G and H are the arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means of two different positive numbers. Which is true?
x: For unequal positive numbers A > G > H, and also G² = AH, so G lies between A and H. Check with 1 and 4: A = 2.5, G = 2, H = 8/5 = 1.6.

q: Sana spends Rs. 600 on mangoes at Rs. 200 per kg, and another Rs. 600 on mangoes at Rs. 300 per kg. What is her average price per kg?
x: Equal amounts of money at two prices give the harmonic mean of the prices: 2 × 200 × 300/(200 + 300) = 240. Check: she buys 3 kg + 2 kg = 5 kg for Rs. 1200, i.e. Rs. 240 per kg. The arithmetic mean 250 is the usual slip.

q: Distinct positive numbers a, b, c are in H.P. Then a/(b + c), b/(c + a), c/(a + b) are in
x: Reciprocals: (b + c)/a = (a + b + c)/a − 1, and similarly for the others. Since 1/a, 1/b, 1/c are in A.P., so are (a + b + c)/a − 1, (a + b + c)/b − 1, (a + b + c)/c − 1, so the given numbers are in H.P. Check with 1, 1/2, 1/3: the reciprocals are 5/6, 8/3, 9/2, with common difference 11/6.

q: What is the sum of the reciprocals of the first 10 terms of the H.P. 1/2, 1/5, 1/8, … ?
x: The reciprocals 2, 5, 8, … form an A.P. with d = 3. Their sum is (10/2)(2 × 2 + 9 × 3) = 5 × 31 = 155. Check: the 10th reciprocal is 29 and 5 × (2 + 29) = 155. Using 10d gives 165.

q: What is the harmonic mean of the roots of x² − 10x + 16 = 0?
x: For roots α, β the harmonic mean is 2αβ/(α + β) = 2 × 16/10 = 16/5. Check: the roots are 2 and 8, and 2 × 2 × 8/10 = 3.2. 5 is their arithmetic mean and 4 their geometric mean.

q: What is the value of Σ (2k + 1) for k = 1 to 10?
x: Σ(2k + 1) = 2Σk + Σ1 = 2 × 55 + 10 = 120. Check: the terms are 3, 5, …, 21, and 10 × (3 + 21)/2 = 120. Forgetting the +1 in every term gives 110.

q: What is the sum of the first 12 terms of the series 1 × 3 + 2 × 5 + 3 × 7 + … ?
x: The nth term is n(2n + 1) = 2n² + n. So S₁₂ = 2 × (12 × 13 × 25/6) + (12 × 13/2) = 2 × 650 + 78 = 1378. Leaving out the Σn part gives 1300.

q: For which positive integer n is 1² + 2² + … + n² equal to 5 times 1 + 2 + … + n?
For some n, 1 + 2 + 3 + … + n = 55. What is 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + … + n³?
x: Σk³ = [n(n + 1)/2]² = (Σk)², so it is 55² = 3025. Check: n(n + 1)/2 = 55 gives n = 10, and 10² × 11²/4 = 3025. 385 is the sum of squares for n = 10.

q: What is the sum of the infinite series 1 + 3/2 + 5/4 + 7/8 + … ?
x: S = 1 + 3x + 5x² + … with x = 1/2. Then S − xS = 1 + 2x + 2x² + … = 1 + 2x/(1 − x), so S(1 − x) = 1 + 2 = 3 and S = 3/(1/2) = 6. Check with the formula (1 + x)/(1 − x)² = 1.5/0.25 = 6. Stopping at S(1 − x) = 3 gives 3.

q: What is the value of Σ (−1)ᵏ · k for k = 1 to 20?
x: Pair the terms: (−1 + 2) + (−3 + 4) + … + (−19 + 20) is 10 pairs, each 1, so the sum is 10. Check: even terms sum to 110 and odd terms to 100, and 110 − 100 = 10. Starting with a + sign gives −10.

q: What is the value of 1 × 10 + 2 × 9 + 3 × 8 + … + 10 × 1?
x: The kth term is k(11 − k) = 11k − k², so the sum is 11 × 55 − 385 = 605 − 385 = 220. Check with n(n + 1)(n + 2)/6 for n = 10: 10 × 11 × 12/6 = 220. 385 is Σk² alone.
